evidence: Project has a single entry point (__main__.py) with unified bot execution, indicating one deployable artifact
Clear separation into logical modules (modules/, services/, db/, utils/, Addons/) with hierarchical directory structure (max depth 4)
Modules are interdependent but co-deployed; no inter-process/network communication between logical components
Service layer (services/) abstracts external dependencies (Mongo, Redis, Pyrogram, Telethon) consistently used across modules
Shared utilities (utils/) and helpers are reused across modules, typical of monolithic designs
Data persistence handled via both SQL (SQLAlchemy) and NoSQL (MongoDB, Odmantic) within the same process space
Event-driven command handling via decorators and registered handlers across modules, but within single runtime
Multiple Telegram clients (Pyrogram/Telethon) integrated directly as libraries, not via external services
No evidence of network boundaries, service discovery, or inter-service communication patterns
risks: Tight coupling between modules increases risk of cascading changes and regression
Scaling requires full application replication rather than component-level scaling
Testing complexity grows with module interdependencies
Single point of failure for the entire bot functionality
Potential for module dependency cycles given high average fan-out (3.6)
